system_description.narrative_title: AI boom vs safety, finance and geopolitics
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid commercial AI build-out is driving market fervour, novel finance and concentration in compute providers while exposing safety failures, corporate governance strains and new geopolitical frictions. The system is open: capital, compute, talent and data flow across firms and borders, creating feedback loops between investment, deployment, security incidents and policy responses. That interaction is producing financialisation of compute (leases, chip offloads, futures, insurance), visible safety incidents and resignations, and state-level regulatory and strategic reactions.
system_description.scope: AI model development and deployment; compute supply chain (chips, datacenters, licensing and leasing); capital markets and financing instruments tied to AI compute (investor offloads, futures, insurance); corporate governance and safety teams; national policy and regulatory responses; media and public sentiment.
system_description.super_system: Global techno‑economic‑political system (international markets, strategic competition—notably US–China—and critical infrastructure)
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and investment vehicles
International trade and supply chains (semiconductors, manufacturing, data centres)
Labor markets, social norms and public opinion

variables.name: AI capability level
variables.description: The aggregate technical performance and generalization ability of leading AI models and architectures available for deployment.

variables.name: Compute capacity available
variables.description: The total accessible high-performance compute (training and inference) across datacenters and leased resources per unit time.

variables.name: Compute price
variables.description: The unit cost of procuring high-performance compute (e.g., GPU/TPU-hour) for model training and inference.

variables.name: Capital flows into AI
variables.description: The rate and scale of financial investment directed toward AI development, compute financing, and AI-linked instruments.

variables.name: Financialization of compute
variables.description: The extent to which compute resources are packaged, traded, insured or otherwise treated as financial assets and instruments.

variables.name: Compute provider concentration
variables.description: The market share concentration of a small number of providers in the supply of high-end compute resources.

variables.name: Corporate safety and governance robustness
variables.description: The overall strength of organizational structures, processes and resourcing dedicated to AI risk management and governance.

variables.name: Safety incident rate
variables.description: The frequency of observable safety, security or misuse events linked to deployed AI systems per unit time.

variables.name: Rogue agent misuse incidence
variables.description: The rate at which autonomous or agentic AI behaviours are exploited, go rogue, or cause covert malicious actions.

variables.name: Regulatory stringency
variables.description: The strictness and scope of legal and policy constraints applied to AI development, deployment and related markets.

variables.name: Geopolitical AI rivalry intensity
variables.description: The intensity of interstate strategic competition and policy friction specifically tied to AI capabilities, supply chains and standards.

variables.name: Talent mobility rate
variables.description: The flow rate of skilled AI researchers, engineers and technical talent across firms and national borders.

variables.name: Cross-border data flow volume
variables.description: The throughput of training-relevant data moving between jurisdictions and organizations available for model development.

variables.name: Public trust and fear
variables.description: The aggregate level of public confidence, concern or fear about AI technologies and their societal impacts.

variables.name: Media attention intensity
variables.description: The volume and tempo of news and commentary covering AI developments, incidents and policy debates per unit time.

variables.name: Investor concentration
variables.description: The degree to which financial exposures and portfolio weight are concentrated in a small set of AI-exposed assets or firms.

catalysts.title: OpenAI turmoil and IPO delay
catalysts.description: Ongoing corporate safety incidents, employee departures and model cancellations are driving OpenAI to delay an IPO and face legal scrutiny, shifting investor and public confidence.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Sam Altman says OpenAI will delay its IPO...", "OpenAI safety employee quits...", "OpenAI axes next model citing safety issues"

catalysts.title: White House AI task force recommendations and AI czar actions
catalysts.description: The newly formed US AI task force and incoming AI czar are expected to publish strategic guidance and regulatory recommendations that could tighten US AI policy and export/control posture.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "White House forms AI task force...", "Trump Expected to Name ODNI’s Jay Clayton as AI Czar", "Exclusive | New AI Czar Unveils Goals"

catalysts.title: Emergence of futures/financial markets for AI compute
catalysts.description: Moves to securitize and create futures/markets for chips and compute capacity (chip offloads, insurance arrangements) accelerate the financialization of compute.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "The coming futures market in AI compute", "Amazon seeks to offload $8bn of Nvidia chips to investors", "Nvidia turns to insurers to spread the risk"

catalysts.title: Rising lawsuits and enforcement actions targeting AI firms
catalysts.description: Uncovered hacks, legal exposures and allegations against major AI firms are likely to trigger additional lawsuits, regulatory probes and enforcement actions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Legal risks pile up for Altman...", "OpenAI uncovers dozens of hacks", "OpenAI alerts more than 100 groups about rogue AI agent activity"

catalysts.title: National-level bans on AI glasses / wearables
catalysts.description: Norway's proposal to temporarily ban AI glasses in some public places could prompt similar local restrictions and product compliance actions in other jurisdictions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Norway is first to propose temporary ban on AI glasses in public places", "Norway to propose temporary ban on AI glasses in some public places"

catalysts.title: China expands compute via large chip leases and domestic build-out
catalysts.description: Chinese firms leasing large chip inventories and domestic infrastructure investments will raise domestic compute capacity and intensify AI strategic competition.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "China’s Tencent leases 100,000 chips from Oracle to accelerate AI push", "Reflection AI boosts US ambition to compete with Chinese ‘open’ models"

catalysts.title: Institutional investors de-risk AI concentration
catalysts.description: Pension funds and large investors cutting US equity exposure over AI concentration risk will drive portfolio rebalancing and fundraising into alternative AI plays and geographies.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Global pension funds cut US equities over AI concentration risk", "Investors look to shelter portfolios from rising AI concentration risks"
